features.title: Manage persistent agents
features.summary: Create, edit, enable, duplicate and remove agents — handle, name, glyph, description, instructions, Agent preset, model route and reasoning effort — from one Host-owned registry every browser and agent reads. The panel lists each agent with its glyph, handle, model and an enable switch; the editor groups identity, instructions, model and tools, delegation, and memory and routine, checks fields inline with a fix for each problem, and asks before dropping unsaved edits; a new agent can start from a template; removal asks first and offers Undo. An agent keeps the threads it started (history and usage survive a Host restart), an optional routine line rides the opening message while the panel reads the reminders back from the Host's schedule catalog, and delegation targets constrain which Agents that agent's threads may message. On a phone the list and the editor take the whole pane in turn. A built-in @dsh agent ships with the harness defaults and cannot be deleted. Thread rows in the thread sidebar show the @handle of the agent that started the thread (agents.threadHandles), falling back to the preset chip.

features.title: Mention an agent where a thread starts
features.summary: A leading @handle dispatches an ordinary thread on that agent: its preset, its model route, its instructions and the user's text as the opening prompt. The dispatch stays where it was — the backlog reports the new thread in a toast whose Open action shows it — the @ menu lists enabled agents, @agent:/@a: narrows it, another source's scope stays empty, and a backlog comment box completes agent handles inline without hijacking @b:/@t:/@f:.
failureModes: An unknown handle stays a plain comment.
A disabled agent is not offered and does not dispatch.
A catalog without the agent's route leaves the Host default model.

features.title: Preview an agent from its mention
features.summary: Every rendered @{handle} reference (and legacy @handle mention) that names a saved agent becomes a link: clicking it (or pressing Enter) opens a card above the reference with the agent's glyph, name, description, model route, tool preset, memory scope, delegation, routine, instructions and its recent threads, and an Open in Agents action selects it in the panel. The card follows the reference while the conversation scrolls; an unknown, removed or misspelled handle stays plain text, so an email address or a menu scope never becomes a link.

features.title: An agent decides its threads' tools
features.summary: Each agent stores which tools and tool groups (an MCP server, a plugin, DSH's own) are disabled or pinned, and which agents its subagents may run as (applied by the subagent tool, see subagent-agents). Every thread gets an agent once, when it attaches: the agent that dispatched it, its parent's agent for a subagent, the project's default agent, else @dsh. The agents plugin provides @dshfiles/tool-search/access with it, and a thread can be overridden with another agent's tools or every tool from its next request. Agent and project-default edits reach threads started afterwards.

features.title: A subagent starts as a configured agent
features.summary: The agents plugin provides @dshfiles/tool-subagent/agent-resolver: the subagent tool's agent argument, else the calling agent's subagents.default, names the agent a fresh child starts as. The calling agent's subagents.allowed must list it (or be any, or name the caller's own agent); unknown, disabled or unlisted handles are refused with the handles involved and agents_subagents_set. The child gets the agent's route, preset and a bounded preamble, and its Session is recorded as the agent's explicit thread before it exists, so tool-search applies that agent's tools from its first request. list_subagent_models lists the agents a caller may start.
